summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.3P completed one read-only strategic architecture reassessment. It re-derived the current public runtime/provider/trust architecture from source and used the production session bootstrap prompt path as the concrete handoff probe. Runtime Registry is an in-memory metadata prototype; runtime inspect creates a fresh empty instance, so canonical current state is 0 plugins, 0 capabilities, no runnable target, Observed / observe / unavailable. Agent/session identity, producer provenance, runtime/backend identity, provider identity, model identity, and OS execution principal are separate; current labels and locks are descriptive and not authenticated dispatch authority. Codex-Ox remains a first-class descriptive session/producer identity with generic intake compatibility but no PCAE-native runtime, OpenRouter transport, provider/model authentication, or invocation mapping. Bootstrap prompt generation is production-consumed but its output is transient stdout and current human copy/paste implicitly combines content acceptance, target selection, and dispatch. Automatic handoff needs immutable prompt/task/repo binding, explicit prompt/target approval, canonical selection and live capability/auth facts, PB dispatch/network permission, final Runtime Enforcement, supervision/confinement, durable invocation/attempt identity, normalized untrusted result, audit, budgets, retry/idempotency, and generic intake linkage. Critical finding: several legacy public CLI paths can invoke subprocesses outside the canonical Runtime Registry/PB/Runtime Enforcement boundary, so canonical execution_unavailable is not a repository-wide interlock. Recommended Option C: trusted PCAE kernel owns authority/state/audit/intake binding while replaceable external bridges own transport only; registry remains metadata/discovery. First later adapter should be deterministic mock/dry. Exact next phase: 149O.20L.7O.3Q Runtime Surface Reconciliation and Runtime / Provider Adapter Contract Freeze, contract-only and not begun. Human decision required. Execution activation NO; mature S/M capability consumption remains EXHAUSTED; v0.4.3 remains public baseline; article STOPPED.
